why: It reads like a finished ticket, but the things a CSV export lives or dies on are absent: which columns in which order, the header row, date and money formats, how commas and quotes in values are escaped, what an empty result looks like, and any row limit. Two engineers would produce two incompatible files.

task.summary: Add a button to the orders page that downloads the current list of orders as a CSV file.

story.role: a finance analyst reconciling monthly sales
story.want: to download the orders I am looking at as a spreadsheet file
story.benefit: I can reconcile them against bank statements without copying rows by hand

task.goal: Let users export orders to CSV.

acceptance.behavior: Clicking the button downloads a CSV of the orders.
acceptance.gherkin:
Given a user on the orders page
When they click "Export CSV"
Then a CSV file containing the orders is downloaded

acceptance.behavior: The export respects the current filters.
acceptance.gherkin:
Given the orders page is filtered to March
When the user clicks "Export CSV"
Then the file contains only the filtered orders

testCases.description: GET /orders/export returns a response with content type text/csv.

scenarios.omitted: Hidden scenarios are not implemented yet.
